subject: Clarification: derivative rights, model-improvement opt-out, and SFTP export runbook
messages:
From: Eva Lawrence <legal@acmeai.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Redwood DPA questions: model training + exportability

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Acme AI is excited about the latency profile. Before we move forward with a pilot, legal needs to confirm a few items for our DPA and procurement checklist. Could you confirm the following and provide any evidence artifacts you have: 

1) Model-improvement opt-out: Can Redwood contractually commit to not use Acme-generated prompts/responses to improve models used in the hosted service (i.e., a learning-exclusion or "no-train" commitment)? If so, please point to the exact DPA language you propose.

2) Derivative/response ownership: Does Acme retain exclusive rights to prompt/response content and derivatives generated during our use? We need clarity for our IP counsel.

3) Subprocessors & cross-border transfers: Please provide a current subprocessor inventory and indicate which subprocessors (if any) process data outside the US or reship to third parties.

4) Export / evidence: For audit purposes we need an onboarding/export runbook (SFTP/API) and a sample export log demonstrating how tenant data and generated responses can be extracted. If you have a checklist or Service Operation Note that we can attach to the DPA, please share.

Attachments: Acme will attach a marked-up DPA once we have your proposed language.

Goal: we’d like a short package (DPA language + evidence pack + runbook) by end of week so procurement can schedule a SOC review next Wednesday.

Appreciate it —
Eva
Legal Operations
Acme AI

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Eva Lawrence <legal@acmeai.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA questions: model training + exportability

Hi Eva — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below, and we’ll follow up with a short evidence pack and a proposed DPA amendment.

1) Model-improvement opt-out: Yes — we can offer a contractual opt-out that prevents customer-provided prompts and generation outputs from being used to train or improve models in the hosted shared model pool. The commitment covers both automated model training and human-in-the-loop data ingestion for improvement. We typically implement this as: 
  - Contract clause: "Provider will not use Customer Data (including prompts and generated outputs) to train or improve models used to serve other customers; Provider will only use Customer Data as necessary to provide the service, and will not incorporate Customer Data into model training datasets without Customer's prior written consent."
  - Operational guardrails: explicit routing to opt-out tenant namespace, disabled long-term training pipelines, and redacted telemetry for opt-out tenants.

2) Derivative/response ownership: We can confirm that customers retain ownership of prompts and responses as data under our standard DPA; we offer an explicit output-licensing addendum for customers who need additional exportability/derivative assurances.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: Attached to this thread is our current subprocessor inventory and a document listing which subprocessors handle cross-border processing. Most core inference happens in our US regions by default; we can route traffic to EU/APAC regions for data locality if requested.

4) Export / evidence: Attaching an "evidence pack" (redwood_evidence_pack_v1.zip) that contains: subprocessor inventory, SOC2 summary, sample audit logs (anonymized), and a SFTP onboarding checklist (sftp_onboarding_checklist.xlsx). The sample export log shows tenant extraction metadata and a one-run CSV sample.

Next steps: 
- We will: (a) prepare a short DPA amendment w/ the model-improvement clause, (b) provide a one-page runbook for SFTP/API export, and (c) schedule a 30min call with SRE if you want to walk the export flow.

Can your team confirm any specific log fields you need in the sample export (e.g., request_id, timestamp, model, prompt_hash, response_id)? We can include those in the runbook sample.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Kimberly and Marissa for contract and evidence follow-up.

—Rishi
Head of Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:08:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Redwood DPA questions: model training + exportability

Kimberly / Marissa — forwarding Eva from Acme. They want a packaged deliverable for procurement: DPA redline with model-improvement opt-out, evidence pack, and SFTP export runbook + sample log. Timeline: end of week.

Can we: 
- Kimberly: draft a DPA amendment w/ the language I suggested and review for any risky phrasing. Include a clause that allows us to route to private/dedicated pools if needed.
- Marissa: assemble the evidence pack (attached files are the start). Please add a concise note describing how we segregate opt-out tenants (namespaces, kv cache retention policy), and confirm retention window for audit logs.
- Ops/SRE: (cc’d on separate thread) we’ll need a quick sample export run and a statement of typical export SLA / retention.

Also, legal is asking for proof of exportability — include a sanitized sample export CSV and a redacted log showing request_id + timestamp + object keys.

Thanks — timing is tight, happy to take a short call with Acme on Wed afternoon.

> On Mon, 15 Jun 2026 at 13:12 Eva Lawrence <legal@acmeai.com> wrote:
> > Hi Rishi,
> > 
> > Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Acme AI is excited about the latency profile...

From: Eva Lawrence <legal@acmeai.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmeai.com>, procurement@acmeai.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA questions: model training + exportability

Rishi / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few follow-ups after a quick review of the evidence pack: 

• DPA language: the proposed clause looks good to our counsel, but they asked for an explicit definition of "Customer Data" that lists prompts, responses, and derived artifacts. Can you add that definition to the amendment?

• Sample export log: the CSV you included is helpful. Can you also provide a redacted sample that shows a full response payload (still redacted) and the associated request_id so our engineers can validate mapping?

• Retention SLA: procurement needs confirmation that audit logs for export runs are retained for at least 90 days and that a one-time export can be completed within 48 hours of request for pilot accounts. Please confirm and put SLA language in the runbook.

• Subprocessors: can you indicate which subprocessors process derivative artifacts specifically (if any)? We need to route this through our privacy team.

If you can send an updated DPA redline and the redacted sample export by EOD tomorrow, procurement will start DocuSign and SOC scheduling. We are OK to proceed with the pilot contingent on these items. 

Thanks again — would like to lock a Wed 11am call to walk the runbook if that works for you.

Best,
Eva
Legal Operations
Acme AI
